about: Texts of the Welcome to Lucciola window (/usr/libexec/margine/welcome), drawn in this order. Edit them with `just edit` (tools/content-editor). Commands go between ` marks.
intro: Welcome. Here is what is worth knowing on the first day; the guide has the rest.

blocks.text: Super is the key with the Windows logo. Windows open side by side in columns, on a strip that runs past the edge of the screen: the keys move you along it.

blocks.text: Lucciola updates itself in the background. You only restart.

items: The system: every day the new version downloads and waits next to the one you run. A notification tells you when it is ready, and it starts at your next restart.
Apps: twice a day, except when the battery is low or the connection is metered.
A way back: every update keeps the previous version. If one goes wrong, restart and choose the second entry in the boot menu.

blocks.text: Lucciola System, in the dock, shows your version and whether a newer one is waiting. From there you can update now, check the system or go back a version. It never restarts the computer by itself.

Homebrew does not come with Lucciola. Apps come from Bazaar, and command-line tools go in a Toolbox (`toolbox create`, then `toolbox enter`). If you install Homebrew yourself, Lucciola upgrades its packages once a week and Lucciola System lists the ones waiting.
Bazaar, the app store in the dock, installs apps from Flathub.
On the first start the apps that come with Lucciola download in the background, so some may be missing for a few minutes. GIMP, Inkscape, darktable and OBS Studio are the largest and arrive last.

At the next restart a blue screen appears before Lucciola starts. Press a key within 10 seconds, choose Enroll MOK, Continue and Yes, type the password `margine` and choose Reboot. That screen uses a US keyboard layout. This registers Lucciola's key, so the system can start with Secure Boot on.
The Lucciola Guide, in the dock, covers the rest: updates, going back to a previous version, disk unlock and where to ask for help. A copy ships with the system, so it opens without a network.
Lucciola is experimental and made by one person. If something does not work, write to me: the guide's help section says how.

footer.text: Once closed, this window does not come back by itself. To see it again, press Super Space and look for Lucciola Welcome.
